title: An Empirical Preregistered Evaluation of Generate–Validate–Repair for Intent-to-Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1) that compares LLM-only configuration generation to a guarded generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline for intent-to-configuration NetOps tasks. Using a frozen plan, a Dockerized Mininet emulation, a deterministic validator, and gpt-5-mini, we ran 200 stratified paired trials (5 protocol groups × 2 modalities × ≈20 tasks) with fully archived artifacts and hashes. Observed outcomes: baseline (LLM-only) = 200/200 verifier-accepted configurations; GVR = 200/200. The paired difference in the operational-failure indicator = 0.00 (95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.00]; 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); exact test p = 1.0. The preregistered power assumption (baseline failure > 0) was not met; the null outcome therefore reflects the tested boundary conditions (shared-initial-candidate generation semantics, synthetic vendor-like templates, deterministic validator, single model) rather than a general claim that GVR is unnecessary. We publish full preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, validator traces, analysis code, and immutable initial-master-prompt reference (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

sections.introduction: Motivation. Large language models can translate operator intent into device configuration, promising automation gains in NetOps. However, unguarded LLM outputs can produce configurations that violate reachability, policy, or availability requirements. Generate–validate–repair (GVR) architectures seek to limit operational risk by adding deterministic validation and bounded repair loops. Research gap. Prior work has proposed benchmarks and verifier-assisted pipelines (NetConfEval, OpsEval, NetEval) but few studies provide preregistered, artifact-backed paired comparisons that (a) freeze design before execution, (b) publish full execution traces and hashes, and (c) make explicit the boundary conditions that determine whether the GVR intervention yields measurable benefit. Research question and contributions. We preregistered (GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1) and executed a paired experiment asking: does a guarded GVR pipeline measurably reduce operational-failure rates (reachability loss or policy violation) relative to LLM-only generation for intent-to-configuration tasks under a controlled emulator and deterministic validator? Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered paired confirmatory run (n=200 pairs) with frozen analysis plan and published artifacts; (2) deterministic reconciliation of execution accounting and per-episode hashes; (3) publication-ready, artifact-grounded reporting of a null paired difference and an explicit accounting of why that null arose under the study boundary conditions.
sections.related_work: Positioning. Existing NetOps/intent-to-configuration evaluations (e.g., Wang et al. NetConfEval 2024; Liu et al. OpsEval 2023; Miao et al. NetEval 2023) established the need for task banks and verifiers. Work on verifier-assisted generation and GVR patterns is common in AIOps literature; however, claims about operational benefits often lack preregistration, deterministic audit trails, or paired within-task designs that avoid sampling confounds. Our study adopts the generate–validate–repair conception but emphasizes preregistration, deterministic validation, and full artifact publication to clarify when GVR produces measurable gains.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and freeze. The preregistration (GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1) froze the research question, estimands (paired difference in binary operational-failure indicator), sampling plan (200 stratified paired tasks), metrics, validator policy, contamination rules (≥80% token overlap threshold), retry policy, and analysis plan (paired bootstrap 10,000 resamples, seed=1729; preregistered Wilcoxon signed-rank as the planned confirmatory test). The preregistration identifier and full JSON are recorded within the execution artifacts (preregistration id GVR-ProtocolEval-2026-PR1; see execution_manifest entries). Execution harness. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Model: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version; execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 a40e96e2...). Emulation and validator. We used a Dockerized Mininet testbed and a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) that parses, normalizes, enforces declared workflow constraints (e.g., "must be down for MTU/VLAN change"), executes reachability probes and policy/ACL checks, and returns a binary verify-accept/verify-reject decision. Task bank and sampling. Confirmatory bank: 200 intent-to-configuration tasks stratified across five protocol/focus groups and two interaction modalities (CLI, API), ≈20 tasks per cluster (task_manifest.jsonl; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 c1bd4a09...). Shared-generation semantics. Per the preregistration and adapter contract the generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false): for each task a single LLM-produced candidate was stored and evaluated under both arms (baseline and guarded). This choice is archived in the execution manifest and explains model-call accounting (one model call per task; model_calls_used = 200, planned_episode_count = 400). Contamination detection and exclusions. Automated contamination checks (token-overlap) were applied per the preregistered rule; no confirmatory tasks exceeded the threshold (analysis/contamination_summary.csv). Analysis. Primary estimand: paired mean difference (GVR − baseline) in the binary operational-failure indicator; estimation by paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, fixed seed = 1729). The preregistration planned a Wilcoxon signed-rank test; the archived confirmatory analysis executed an exact paired contingency check (McNemar) on the observed contingency table and recorded exact p-values; both archived test outputs are reported below with artifact pointers.
sections.results: Execution summary (artifact-backed). All planned episodes completed (planned model-call budget = 400; model_calls_used = 200; completed episodes = 400; no infrastructure failures). Confirmatory outcomes (archived scoring CSVs and JSONs): complete paired tasks = 200; baseline verifier-accepted = 200/200; guarded verifier-accepted = 200/200. Paired contingency: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, SHA-256 7bc1bd2a...). Paired estimate and inference. Paired difference (guarded minus baseline) = 0.00. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Statistical tests and reconciliation. The preregistered primary test was the Wilcoxon signed-rank (planned). The reconciled archived confirmatory output contains an exact paired contingency assessment (exact McNemar two-sided) reported by the deterministic analysis executor (analysis results artifact shows exact_mcnemar_two_sided, p = 1.0). The Wilcoxon-signed-rank outcome reported in the manuscript artifacts is consistent with the contingency-based result for this degenerate contingency (p = 1.0); all test outputs and the analysis log are archived (analysis/* CSVs and analysis_log.jsonl). Repair activity and iteration statistics (preregistered exploratory items). No repair invocation occurred for any confirmatory task: repair_attempts = 0 across 200 tasks. Consequently repair-iteration counts are zero for all confirmatory pairs. This is observable in the provider-call traces and scoring JSONs where no repair-provider trace path or repair_prompt_sha256 appears (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json shows repair_applied: false; provider traces are under execution/provider_calls/*. Representative artifacts and hashes. Example tasks and identical-baseline/guarded response hashes (archived): task-000001 shared/baseline/guarded response hash f8de4d6e1a625e42... (execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt; scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/); task-000002 response hash ae967f70dfb6cc...; task-000003 response hash f7f4db249ecbb...; full per-episode response hashes and the execution_manifest are published (execution_manifest.json artifact list with SHA-256 entries). Contamination and exclusions. Automated contamination detector flagged 0 confirmatory tasks; no exclusions were applied (analysis/contamination_summary.csv). Deterministic reconciliation. All accounting checks (pair counts, model-call accounting, cache metrics) passed (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, analysis artifact).
sections.discussion: Why the confirmatory null outcome occurred (artifact-grounded). The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced exactly one LLM candidate per task that both arms evaluated; because no repairs were triggered on any confirmatory task (repair_attempts = 0), baseline and guarded arms were identical for every task. This design choice is recorded in the preregistration and in the execution manifest (generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate", independent_condition_generation = false) and is the proximal cause of the observed null paired difference. Task and validator scope. The confirmatory bank consisted of synthetic, vendor-inspired templates executed in a controlled Mininet emulator; the deterministic validator enforces explicit workflow constraints and operational checks. Under these narrow, well-specified conditions the LLM (gpt-5-mini) produced verifier-acceptable outputs in every trial. Implications for generality. The null paired difference does not imply that GVR is needless in broader or production settings. Operational scenarios that can produce nonzero baseline failure rates include: (a) open-ended or ambiguous intents, (b) model stochasticity or use of different model families, (c) richer device semantics and firmware diversity absent from the emulator, (d) weaker validators or incomplete verifier-rule coverage, and (e) adversarial or novel fault modes. Practical recommendations for future confirmatory designs (artifact-aware): (1) when the scientific target is the incremental value of repairs, preregister independent-condition-generation (produce separate LLM candidates per arm) so repairs can differ; (2) ensure baseline nonzero failure rates in pilot data or adjust sample size/power plans accordingly; (3) expand model and validator diversity for external validity mapping. Reproducibility and transparency. We publish the complete preregistration, execution manifest, raw model responses, provider-call traces, validator traces, scoring JSONs, analysis scripts, and deterministic reconciliation artifacts; key artifact paths and SHA-256 values are recorded in the execution_manifest.json and in the Disclosure Statement below. These artifacts suffice to replicate the reported counts and the deterministic arithmetic in this report.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a fully preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation comparing LLM-only generation and a guarded GVR pipeline on 200 stratified intent-to-configuration tasks in a deterministic emulated environment using gpt-5-mini. Both arms produced verifier-accepted configurations on every confirmatory task (200/200), yielding a paired difference of 0.00 (95% CI [0.00, 0.00]) and exact-test p = 1.0. The null outcome arises from preregistered shared-generation semantics (one LLM candidate per task evaluated under both arms) and the constrained task/validator scope; accordingly the study maps a concrete boundary condition in which GVR did not alter verifier acceptance, rather than proving that GVR is unnecessary in more general or production settings. All artifacts, hashes, and analysis code are published in the execution manifest to enable reproducible reanalysis and follow-up experiments that relax the shared-generation constraint, widen model diversity, and expand verifier coverage.

Limitations summary (see manuscript Limitations section for full discussion): constrained emulation and synthetic task scope; single-model evaluation; preregistered shared-generation semantics limited the opportunity for repairs to produce differing guarded outcomes; deterministic validator coverage is finite and may not reflect production device semantics; observed baseline success = 100% invalidated the preregistered power assumption targeted at nonzero baseline failure. All archived artifacts, provider traces, validator traces, raw outputs, and analysis scripts are published in the execution bundle with SHA-256 hashes recorded in execution_manifest.json to enable deterministic reproduction of the reported arithmetic and counts.
limitations: Emulation and synthetic task scope: confirmatory bank used synthetic vendor-inspired templates executed in Dockerized Mininet; external validity to production devices and firmware diversity is limited.
Single-model evaluation: only gpt-5-mini was tested in the confirmatory experiment; results do not generalize across model families or stochastic sampling regimes.

Shared-generation preregistered semantics: generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false) produced one LLM candidate per task that both arms evaluated; because no repairs were invoked (repair_attempts = 0) baseline and guarded outputs were identical for every confirmatory task, limiting the ability to measure incremental repair benefit in this run.

Validator coverage constraints: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite rule set and emulator probes; it cannot represent all production device behaviors, stateful middleboxes, or hardware-specific failure modes.

Power-plan assumption violated: preregistered power targeted detecting an absolute paired reduction but assumed baseline failures; observed baseline = 100% success, so the confirmatory null is uninformative outside the tested boundary conditions.

Contamination detection limits: automated token-overlap checks (≥80% threshold) flagged 0 confirmatory tasks, but undiscoverable overlap between model pretraining data and task templates cannot be ruled out.
